title: PES 0110 writes stem, candlewick and chain lines as PE-DESIGN's line types
description: design.export with pesVersion 11 writes three 20 mm squares, region off, with a Stem, a Candlewick and a Chain line in Red, as CEmbLine objects with PE-DESIGN's line codes at +44 (5, 6, 8) and the +86 value of PE-DESIGN's own files (0, 0, 1: line-stem-default, line-candlewick-default, line-chain-default in compat/reference/stitches). The start and end options of these types are written at PE-DESIGN's defaults, and the sewing end PE-DESIGN picks on a closed outline is not mapped (the writer writes the end of the last segment). Reference: PE-DESIGN 11.50 should open the file with the three lines editable and their types shown.

evidence.note: docs/FILE_FORMATS.md, PES 0110 line types: the codes at +44 and +86 read from the owner's 22 line-* files (compat/reference/stitches); the writer's rewrite of those files is byte-identical outside the documented differences (written_object_sections_match_pe_designs_bytes_outside_the_documented_differences)

references.make: Run `stitchtool compat --only pes-0110-line-types` and open target/compat/work/pes-0110-line-types/a.pes in PE-DESIGN 11 (App menu > Open). Expected: three 20 mm squares, region not sewn, each an editable shape; selecting each shows the line sew type Stem Stitch, Candlewick Stitch and Chain Stitch in 800 RED. Record in the MANIFEST notes whether the file opens and with what warning, each line's sew type and attributes as shown, and the status-bar size and stitch count. Then Save As PES, default type (Layout & Editing Ver.11.0 File, #PES0110), unchanged, under the file name given, and record the PE-DESIGN version, the date, the operating system and every setting in compat/reference/MANIFEST.json (see docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md). If PE-DESIGN refuses the file or opens it blank, do not add a file: write what you saw in the notes of docs/COMPATIBILITY_TESTS.md instead.
